rules.label: Presumptive eligibility - 100% write-off based on life circumstances
rules.quote: Presumptive eligibility may be determined on the basis of individual life circumstances that may include: State-funded prescription programs; Homeless or received care from a homeless clinic; Participation in Women, Infants and Children programs (WIC); Food stamp eligibility; Subsidized school lunch program eligibility

payment_plan.quote: If the patient/guarantor qualifies for a reduction in liability, he/she will be notified of payment arrangements made for the non-write-off amount

notes: Policy references NH RSA 151:12-b, IRS Section 501(r), and ACA 2010 - this is a New Hampshire/Vermont hospital, not Colorado
Excluded services: Elective cosmetic procedures, Hearing Aids and repairs, DOT Examinations, Sports Physicals, Gait Analysis, Dry Needling (Exhibit A)

Providers accepting VRH Financial Assistance: All employed providers of VRH including VRH owned physician clinics, Dartmouth Hitchcock, Medstream Anesthesia LLC, BlueWater Emergency Partners. Independent providers NOT accepting: Keady Family Practice, Charlestown Family Medicine (Exhibit C)

Appeals process: Patient can appeal denial within 30 days by writing to Director of Revenue Cycle; appeal reviewed by Revenue Cycle Director not involved in original decision; final decision within 30 days
Application must be returned within 10 days of receipt; failure to comply may result in denial
100% charity applicants notified within 30 days of receipt of application
Falsification of application or refusal to cooperate results in denial of charity benefits
Financial Assistance extended past expiration date to include hospital stays that begin while covered under the Financial Assistance Program
Patients on fixed incomes (e.g., Social Security) must reapply each year

Hospital will not impose extraordinary collections actions without first making reasonable efforts to determine eligibility for financial assistance; exceptions require Revenue Cycle Director and/or CFO approval
Refunds: If patient paid balance and subsequently submits approved application, hospital will refund amount paid
Sheltered assets not counted: Savings/CDs/checking up to $5,000 per person/$10,000 per family; Equity in primary residence up to $100,000 ($150,000 for applicants 55+)
Due to 501(r)(6) lien limitations, homeowners not required to apply for Medicaid prior to financial assistance approval
Determination of financial need may occur at any point in the collection cycle
All insurance payments and contractual adjustments as well as the uninsured discount are taken prior to the financial assistance adjustment being applied
Uninsured patients may not be charged more than amount generally billed to insured patients for same care
Uninsured discount based on 'Look Back' method per 501(r) regulations, applied prior to billing and prior to financial assistance adjustments
Uninsured discount doesn't apply to copayments, coinsurance, deductibles, pre-payment/package services with required discount, or services classified as non-covered by all insurance companies
Valley Regional will share application and supporting documentation with any hospital applicant requests
Income guidelines effective 4/1/25-3/31/26 per Exhibit A
Crisis stabilization services in ER by LCSW considered non-covered by VT Medicaid are eligible for charity
If patient exceeded max ER visits under Medicaid, balance can be adjusted to Financial Assistance at 100%
Deductible and co-insurance amounts eligible for charity if financial circumstances warrant

Individuals with financial capacity to purchase health insurance are required to do so; must demonstrate compliance with NH/VT Healthcare Exchange Program if eligible; exceptions approved by Revenue Cycle Director and/or CFO

notes: Presumptive eligibility may be granted based on circumstances such as homelessness, participation in WIC, food stamp eligibility, or other state/local assistance programs, resulting in a 100% write-off. Presumptive screening is used for accounts >120 days after statements, after collection notices, and prior to referral to outside collection agency. Applications must be verified and applicants must cooperate; falsification or refusal to cooperate results in denial. Financial assistance requires reapplication every 6 months (or annually for fixed incomes like Social Security). The hospital will refund any amount paid if a subsequent approved application is submitted. Extraordinary collection actions require prior reasonable efforts to determine financial assistance eligibility, with exceptions needing approval from Revenue Cycle Director and/or CFO. Exhibit A lists excluded services: elective cosmetic procedures, hearing aids and repairs, DOT examinations, sports physicals, gait analysis, dry needling. Exhibit C lists providers accepting VRH financial assistance: all employed VRH providers and VRH-owned physician clinics, plus Dartmouth Hitchcock, Medstream Anesthesia LLC, and BlueWater Emergency Partners upon request.
